papers.title_en: Towards a knowledge-enhanced single-cell foundation model
papers.authors: Hanqing Zhang, Jie Bao, Mei Ma, Shuai Liu, Jiaying Ma, Jiaguan Liu, Jiaxiao Li, Zhenbo Li, Wenwen Gong, Zhijun Ca
papers.evidence: 知识增强单细胞基础模型，属基因组大模型方向
papers.tldr: 单细胞基础模型多依赖扩大转录组预训练数据，但收益递减且算力成本高。本文提出 scKITE，将细胞注释与基因调控等生物知识作为额外扩展维度，通过轻量辅助解码器融入共享转录组 Transformer 编码器。辅助解码器仅在预训练使用并在下游丢弃，从而得到知识增强的通用编码器。仅用 179,067 个预训练样本，不足以往强模型 0.5%，scKITE 在多项下游任务上仍优于这些模型，表明知识增强预训练是构建生物学基础单细胞基础模型的有前景范式。
papers.abstract_en: Single-cell foundation models (scFMs) increasingly rely on large-scale transcriptomic pretraining, yet expanding pretraining data can yield diminishing gains while substantially increasing computational cost. Our data scaling analyses showed that incorporating biological knowledge, including cell-level text annotation and gene-level regulatory information, provided additional scaling dimension than simply increasing data size. Motivated by this observation, we present scKITE, a simple yet effective scFM that integrates cell-annotation and gene-regulatory supervision into a shared transcriptomic Transformer encoder through lightweight auxiliary decoders. These decoders are used only during pretraining and subsequently discarded, yielding a general-purpose encoder enriched with biological knowledge for downstream applications. With only 179,067 pretraining samples, i.e., less than 0.5\% of those used by previous strong scFMs, scKITE outperformed these models across diverse downstream tasks, highlighting knowledge-enhanced pretraining as a promising paradigm for biologically grounded scFMs.
